text: dsh-plugin-heartbeat（DSH Web 插件）：为根会话提供按信号触发的自主心跳。它比较待办、团队任务、目标和未答问题的变化，并按静默时段、去重和预算决定是否发送提醒。用户可在面板查看状态、暂停或手动触发检查。适合希望 DSH 主动跟进重要进展又避免重复打扰的场景；无需 API key，状态保存在本地。

Heartbeat adds signal driven pulses to DSH Web root sessions. It compares task, team, goal, and question changes, then applies quiet hours, deduplication, and budgets before sending prompts. A panel shows status and supports pause or manual checks. No API key is needed; state stays local.

I want DSH to check session tasks periodically and speak only when something changes.
Can I pause proactive follow ups and inspect why recent heartbeat pulses stayed quiet?
dsh-plugin-heartbeat 的功能「变化触发提醒」：比较待办、团队任务、目标和未答问题的会话投影，只把检测到的变化交给后续门控；重复状态不会每次脉冲都转成提醒。
dsh-plugin-heartbeat 的功能「节律与静默控制」：按信号强度和未回应次数计算下一次脉冲，并支持静默时段、递增间隔、去重和预算限制。
dsh-plugin-heartbeat 的功能「状态面板与手动控制」：通过配置、状态和控制接口查看脉冲信息，触发立即检查、暂停、恢复、重置或暂缓一段时间。
想让 DSH 在目标变化时提醒我，而不是重复播报。
I need a quiet periodic check that follows up on changed session goals.

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · dsh-plugin-heartbeat：> An autonomic heartbeat for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): it pulses in silence, reads the session's own projections, and only opens a turn when something actually changed — a report (L1), a decision question (L2), or an escalation (L4). No signal, no message.

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · dsh-plugin-heartbeat：A Cordis plugin for DeepSeek Harness. v0.5 made the heartbeat *task-aware*; **v0.6.0 turns it from a metronome into an autonomic nervous system**: every pulse reads the session silently, measures arousal, and speaks only when there is a reason. When there is nothing to say, the pulse is recorded in its vitals and nothing is injected at all.

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · Heads-up: the default behaviour changed in v0.6.0：- **0.5.x**: one message every `intervalSeconds`, whether or not anything happened (the task snapshot was re-read and repeated).
- **0.6.0**: a **silent pulse** by default — no signal, no turn, no injected message. It speaks at L1/L2/L4 only when it detects a change worth a message (see the level table below).
- The config file is now **v2**: `intervalSeconds` → `baseIntervalSeconds`, plus rhythm / quiet-hours / dedupe / budget / L3 / workspace fields. An existing v1 `heartbeat.json` is **migrated automatically** on load — nothing to do.
- Runtime state now lives in `<dshHome>/heartbeat-vitals.json` (separate from the config, so hand-editing the config never pollutes runtime state). It survives restarts, and after a restart the plugin stays quiet for `restartCooldownSeconds` (default 5 minutes) before it may speak again.
- The settings sidebar label follows the App language — **心跳** in Chinese, **Heartbeat** in English — with the same stroked-heart icon.

text:
dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · How it works：A host-plane Cordis plugin attaches one runtime to every **root agent** (subagents are skipped), including sessions that already exist when the plugin is hot-mounted.

Each pulse runs the same four steps — the plugin itself never asks an LLM to decide:

```
sensors → rhythm → gate → action
```

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · How it works：- **Sensors** (`lib/sensors.js`): synchronously read the session's public projections — `todos`, `agentTeam`, `goal`, `userQuestions`, plus `contextPressure` — and **diff them against what the last pulse saw**. Only changes become signals, each with a weight; the weights sum into an **arousal** score (0–8). Repeating the same todo list on every beat is exactly the noise v0.6 removes.
- **Rhythm** (`lib/rhythm.js`): the next interval is `baseInterval × (1 + missed) × mood(arousal)`, clamped to 30 s – 24 h, where higher arousal shortens the interval (arousal 4 → one third). Quiet hours suspend pulses entirely, a refractory window enforces a minimum silence after a delivery, and a small deterministic jitter stops several sessions from firing on the same tick.
- **Gate** (`lib/gate.js`): decides **L0 (silent) / L1 (report) / L2 (ask) / L4 (escalation)**, applies the dedupe window and the daily budget, and refuses to speak when you just spoke, when context pressure is high, during quiet hours, or while paused/snoozed.
- **Action** (`lib/runtime.js`): for L1/L2/L4 it optionally compacts long history first, then injects one message carrying a **w

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · How it works：**Event-driven beats (new in v0.6)**: when the host exposes `sessionProjections.onChanged`, a change in `todos` / `agentTeam` / `goal` / `userQuestions` marks the session and runs **one extra pulse after a 2 s debounce** — still through every gate (dedupe, budget, quiet hours). Without that service the plugin falls back to pure timer mode.

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · Autonomy levels (L0–L4)：| Level | Behaviour | Default in v0.6 |
|---|---|---|
| **L0** | Silent pulse: read, diff, record — **inject nothing** | ✅ the default for every tick without a signal |
| **L1** | Open a turn and **report** progress / risks / blockers only | ✅ when there are progress-only signals |
| **L2** | Open a turn and **ask** (`ask_user_question`) whether to act / which option | ✅ when a decision-bearing signal appears |
| **L3** | Within **granted categories**, proceed without asking first | ⛔ **off by default** (`l3Allow: []`); instruction-level authorization only |
| **L4** | Same ask as L2 but with **escalated wording** when a decision signal has already gone unanswered (`missed ≥ 2`) — frequency never increases | ✅ |

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · Autonomy levels (L0–L4)：Signals that require a decision (and therefore L2/L4): a team task becoming **ready**, a team task becoming **blocked**, the goal entering **blocked / paused**, and a **pending unanswered user question**. Progress-only signals (a team task completed, todos changing) produce L1.

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · L3 in one paragraph：L3 is a **per-category grant list** — `read` (search / read files), `test` (run tests / lint / build), `notes` (write workspace docs / notes), `continue` (continue an already-agreed draft). It is empty by default, so v0.6 behaves as "ask, never act". When you grant categories, L2/L4 messages carry one extra line authorizing the agent to proceed inside those categories only; everything else still asks first. **L3 is not a sandbox**: publishing, deploying, deleting, `rm`, git push and any external write are never whitelisted, and irreversible operations are still stopped by the host's approval flow. The grant only changes the instruction, not the host's safety checks.

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · Signals, dedupe and budgets：| Signal | Source (projection diff) | Dedupe key | Weight |
|---|---|---|---|
| Team task became ready | `agentTeam` | `team:<id>:ready` | +5 |
| Team task became blocked | `agentTeam` | `team:<id>:blocked` | +4 |
| Goal blocked / paused | `goal` | `goal:<id>:<phase>` | +4 |
| Pending user question | `userQuestions` | `question:<callId>` | +3 |
| Todos changed (open items) | `todos` | `todos:<signature>` | +2 |
| Team task completed | `agentTeam` | — (reported, not deduped) | +1 |

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · Signals, dedupe and budgets：`arousal = clamp(Σ weights, 0, 8)`; as arousal rises the interval shortens.

What suppresses a pulse before it can speak (all in `lib/gate.js`):

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · Signals, dedupe and budgets：The one exception is the panel's **Beat now** button: a manual beat skips the politeness gates (quiet hours, budget, dedupe, "user recently spoke", an active child session) but still picks its level and still checks that the agent has a usable driver surface.

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · Task inspection (the snapshot in the message)：Since v0.5 a beat can carry a compact task snapshot; the sensors reuse the same projections, so the message and the signals cannot disagree.

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · Task inspection (the snapshot in the message)：| Projection | Read | Snapshot rule |
|---|---|---|
| `todos` | session todo list (`content` / `status`) | only `in_progress` / `pending`; `completed` dropped |
| `agentTeam` | Agent Team board (`subject` / `status` / `blockedBy`) | open items only, sorted "ready → in progress → blocked"; blockers named |
| `goal` | persistent goal (`objective` / `phase`) | only `active` / `paused` / `blocked` phases |

text:
dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · Vitals and manual control：| Action | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Beat now** | force one pulse immediately (manual: skips the politeness gates, still picks a level) |
| **Snooze 30m** | no pulses for 30 minutes (`minutes` is configurable through the API, 1–1440) |
| **Pause** | stop this session's heartbeat until resumed |
| **Resume** | lift pause / snooze and re-arm from the current rhythm |
| **Reset** | clear snooze + pause and resume |

Routes (loopback, plugin-owned):

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · Vitals and manual control：| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| GET / POST | `/api/heartbeat/config` | read the v2 config / patch it (validated, hot-applied) |
| GET | `/api/heartbeat/status` | config summary, today's budget, per-session vitals + `nextBeatAt` + last 5 pulses |
| POST | `/api/heartbeat/control` | `{action: "beat-now" \| "snooze" \| "pause" \| "resume" \| "reset", sessionId?, minutes?}` |

Every control action targets the given `sessionId`, or all live sessions when omitted.

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · Vitals and manual control：The panel's wording is localised through DSH's own locale layer: the client half injects `locale`, registers a `heartbeat` namespace with zh/en packs and declares `locale: 'heartbeat'` on the settings section, so the panel follows **Settings → General → Language** and re-renders immediately when you switch the app language (it does not guess from the browser). The sidebar label follows the same setting — 中文「心跳」/ English `Heartbeat` — and the heart-icon claim re-runs after a language switch, so the mark always sits on the current row.

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · Diagnostics (v0.8.0)：The panel can answer "why didn't it say anything?" without digging through logs: a diagnostics block lists the **last 5 pulses** with time, level and **reason** (e.g. `没有新信号`, `静默时段`, `proactive-cooldown（让位给 memory）`, `child-active`), and shows **who currently holds the speech floor** from the status route's new `lock` field — so a quiet run is explainable at a glance. The L3 section also summarises the granted categories instead of only showing the checkboxes.

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · Speech arbitration with other plugins (v0.7.0)：Several proactive plugins may want to speak in the same conversation. v0.7 adds a tiny shared protocol so two of them cannot talk over each other:

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · Physiology line (v0.7.0)：The heartbeat is not a cron job: it has a body. L1/L2/L4 messages can carry one short line right after "why now", e.g. `〔状态：距你上次说话 2h · 今天第 3 次找你〕`:

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · Physiology line (v0.7.0)：`userActiveSuppressSeconds` (default **120**, `0` disables) makes the "you just spoke → stay quiet" window configurable; it uses the persisted `lastUserMessageAt`, so it also holds across restarts.

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · Child activity pill (v0.7.0)：While a background subagent is still running, the conversation header can look finished.

**Known host behaviour this compensates for**: DSH recomputes a session list's `running` flag only when agents are created or disposed, and forwards child `api-session/status` per session resource — while the parent is idle, its view may not receive the child's run-state change, so the header may show "N sub-agents" instead of "running" and the main conversation appears complete.

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · Child activity pill (v0.7.0)：The plugin now reports `children: { total, running, runningIds }` per session on `GET /api/heartbeat/status` (from the `subagentCatalog` / `agentTeam` wire views plus the live agent registry — the same host truth the runtime uses to stay silent), and the client registers a header pill **「子智能体执行中 · N」** in `conversation.session.header.actions`, polling every 5 s; it hides automatically once the children settle and follows the app language. Polling **pauses while the browser tab is hidden** and resumes immediately when you return. **Pure plugin layer — no host change.**

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-plugin-heartbeat
```

(The package declares a `dsh.bundle` manifest, so `dsh plugin add` mounts it into the profile's bundles layer automatically; one-click install in dsh-market uses the same path.)

Restart DSH. Then use **Settings → Heartbeat** to change the mode, interval, quiet hours, dedupe window, budget, L3 grants and task inspection at any time; saving applies hot (no restart).

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · Install：> ⚠️ **Don't** hand-write `- insert: {id: dsh-heartbeat, ...}` into the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`: it collides with the bundle manifest's automatic mount and the whole profile fails to start with
> `duplicate loader entry id "dsh-heartbeat"` (real incident on 2026-08-18, colliding with the memory plugin's entry). Runtime config lives in `<dshHome>/heartbeat.json`; override composition keys (such as `prompt`) with an **id-only override entry, no insert** — see below.

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · Settings sidebar icon：The settings sidebar entry carries a **stroked heart** mark: a 16×16 grid, `stroke-width: 1.3` (the shared `ICON_MEDIUM_STROKE`), pure-black alpha painted through `mask-image` so the visible colour follows `currentColor` in both light and dark themes. It matches the dsh-plugin-memory icon spec exactly. The official `settings.section` slot projects only id / order / label — there is no icon field — so the plugin claims its own nav row by the exact **localized** label text (`心跳` or `Heartbeat`), mirrors it with a `MutationObserver` (re-claimed after a language switch — the claim key changes with the label — or a remount) and cleans everything up on dispose.

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · Version requirements：- **DSH: official 0.2.1-rc.5 series.** `package.json` declares `engines.dsh: "^0.2.1-rc.5"`; the host gates with semver (`includePrerelease: true`), so mind prerelease semantics: `^0.2.1` / `>=0.2.0` **do not match** `0.2.1-rc.5`; only `^0.2.1-rc.5` does. It also covers the eventual 0.2.1 stable, while `0.3.0-rc.1` is judged incompatible.
- **session format v4** (official 0.1.7+). The heartbeat source uses the producer-owned kind `plugin:heartbeat`; v4's native admission rejects the v3 `{kind:'plugin', plugin:'heartbeat'}` wrapper. The v4 and v3 allowlists are mutually exclusive.
- **0.4.2 is the last v3-compatible version**; **from 0.5.0 the plugin supports only the official DSH 0.2.1-rc.5 series**. 0.3.x is not supported yet.
- **Use 0.8.0**: the published 0.6.1 misreads session projections — `stateOf()` returns raw state, so the `subagent` identity `{}` was treated as "this is a subagent" and **no heartbeat attached at all**, while the child-active gate never fired; 0.6.2 fixed that, 0.7.0 added speech-right arbitration, the physiology line and the child-activity pill, and 0.8.0 adds the diagnostics panel, panel controls for the

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · Configuration (v2)：The user config lives in `<dshHome>/heartbeat.json` (written by the panel or by hand; validated with schemastery). Composition config is the base layer, the user file overrides it, and a matching `workspaces` entry overrides both.

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · Configuration (v2)：| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | master switch |
| `mode` | `"assist"` | `"assist"` = speak on signals; `"silent"` = never speak (pulses still run and are recorded) |
| `baseIntervalSeconds` | `600` | base pulse interval (30–86400 s); the per-missed backoff tiers scale from it |
| `pauseAfterMissed` | `3` | hard stop after N unanswered beats (0 = off); your next message revives it |
| `backoffSeconds` | `null` | explicit backoff tier array (`null` = derive `[base, 2×base, 3×base]`) |
| `compactBeforeBeat` | `true` | fold long history into a checkpoint before speaking (best-effort) |
| `maxBeatsPerHour` | `0` | sliding hourly cap on delivered beats (0 = off) |
| `maxBeatsPerDay` | `12` | daily budget of delivered beats (0 = unlimited), shared across sessions in the process |
| `dedupeWindowMinutes` | `90` | never re-ask the same signal key inside this window (0 = off) |
| `refractorySeconds` | `300` | minimum silence after a delivery before the next beat |
| `jitterSeconds` | `60` | deterministic per-session jitter (0–600 s) so sessions spread out |
| `restartCooldownSeconds` | `300` | after a restart,

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · Configuration (v2)：A `workspaces` entry accepts: `enabled`, `mode`, `baseIntervalSeconds`, `quietHours` (object or `null`), `maxBeatsPerDay`, `l3Allow`. Precedence: composition config < user config < matching workspace override.

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · Configuration (v2)：**v1 → v2 migration**: a v1 file (`intervalSeconds`, no `version`) is migrated on load — `intervalSeconds` becomes `baseIntervalSeconds`, the other fields keep their meaning, missing keys take the v2 defaults — and is written back as v2. A corrupt config file is ignored (the last good config stays in memory, defaults on the next start); unrecognised keys are not persisted. Runtime state is separate: `<dshHome>/heartbeat-vitals.json`.

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · Configuration (v2)：Custom heartbeat prompt (composition config, **no `insert`**, to avoid duplicating the bundle layer):

```yaml
- id: dsh-heartbeat
  config:
    prompt: |
      【Heartbeat】{{time}} — why now: {{reason}}

`{{time}}`, `{{tasks}}` and `{{reason}}` are substituted. A template without `{{tasks}}` gets the task block appended; a template without `{{reason}}` gets the why-now line appended.

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · Development：```sh
node --test
```

No-arg `node --test` discovers `test/*.test.mjs`; the suite covers `runtime`, `tasks`, `sensors`, `rhythm`, `gate`, `vitals`, `config-store-v2`, `prompt-levels`, `wiring-v06`, `settings-nav-icon`, `client-half`, `proactive-lock`, `physiology`, `prompt-physiology` and `activity` — **186 tests** at the moment; CI runs the same suite via `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · Development：Design and implementation notes live in the repo (not shipped in the npm package): `docs/specs/2026-10-30-heartbeat-v0.6-design.md` and `docs/plans/2026-10-30-heartbeat-v0.6.md`. The cross-plugin speech-floor protocol is documented publicly in [docs/PROACTIVE-PROTOCOL.md](docs/PROACTIVE-PROTOCOL.md); contrib/security policies are in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

dsh-plugin-heartbeat README · Known limits：- The heartbeat only exists while the DSH process is alive (it stops when the app quits).
- Each root agent has its own runtime; **subagent conversations never get a heartbeat** (identity-guarded — see below).
- **By default the heartbeat is quiet**: if nothing changes, it says nothing. "Presence" now comes from the panel's vitals view and the Beat now button, not from scheduled chatter — raise `mode`/dedupe/quiet settings if you want more voice.
- **Never speaks over delegated work (v0.6.1)**: while a child subagent / teammate session is running, the root agent is idle only because it is waiting. A heartbeat at that moment would inject a new turn mid-work, and the client presents the running child as part of the active turn — the new turn would hide it, so you could no longer tell that background work is still running (and pre-beat compaction could fold the live turn away). Pulses therefore record `L0 · child-active` and inject nothing until every child settles; **Beat now** still forces one beat.
- **The header pill is the reliable “still working” indicator (v0.7.0)**: while children run, the host conversation header may show the parent
